how_applied.method: surgical per-record patch, not a wholesale re-run of run() or the standard build-wta-main-pbp-approved-index.py script
how_applied.why_not_a_wholesale_rerun: A wholesale re-run of run() for 2012-2015 would ALSO apply the 217 demotions the reconciliation audit found as an inseparable side effect of the same matching-code fix, which was explicitly out of scope for this promotion (only the 815 were approved). The patch therefore updates only the exact 815 record keys identified in the audited manifest, using content captured from a real (unmodified) execution of run(), leaving every other record's on-disk content byte-identical to its pre-promotion state.
how_applied.approved_index_build_note: scripts/build-wta-main-pbp-approved-index.py could not be re-run wholesale either: it is a destructive, one-shot tool (it strips reconstructed_games from verified-mappings.json after reading it) and was found to already be broken for any second invocation even before this promotion (the 2011 non-Slam file was already fully stripped from an earlier, pre-existing production run, so any fresh invocation of the script crashes with KeyError on the very first file -- confirmed pre-existing, not introduced by this change; git status after the failed run showed zero additional file changes). The 815 new rows were instead built by importing and calling the same convert_nonslam() function the production script uses, verified to produce byte-identical existing rows plus exactly 815 new ones, and reconstructed_games was then stripped from the newly-appended verified-mappings.json entries to restore the standard on-disk invariant for the future.
